note: To friends, family, anyone younger or close.

term: ありがとうございます。
reading: ありがとうございます
note: The default polite thanks — staff, strangers, seniors.
Textbook reply; in real life many just say いえいえ.
Apology, getting attention, and even thanks — the most used word.
Casual apology to friends and family.
Apologizing for something already done, to a senior or stranger.

reading: もうしわけありません
note: Serious, formal apology at work or from staff.
Reply to someone's apology or thanks.
Reassuring a friend.
Thanking someone for help — warmer than just ありがとう.

term: ごめん、待たせちゃった？
reading: ごめんまたせちゃった
back: Sorry, did I keep you waiting?
note: Arriving to meet a friend.

reading: しんぱいかけてごめんね
note: To family or friends after being ill or out of touch.

term: さっきは言いすぎてごめん。
reading: さっきはいいすぎてごめん
back: Sorry I said too much earlier.
note: Making up after an argument.

term: 聞いてくれてありがとう。
reading: きいてくれてありがとう
note: After venting to a friend.

term: 心配してくれてありがとうね。
reading: しんぱいしてくれてありがとうね
note: To a friend who checked on you.

term: そう言ってくれて嬉しいよ。
reading: そういってくれてうれしいよ
note: Reply to a compliment or kind words.

term: お気遣いありがとうございます。
reading: おきづかいありがとうございます
note: Polite thanks to a colleague or senior who showed care.

term: ご心配をおかけしました。
reading: ごしんぱいをおかけしました
note: Polite version, e.g. returning to work after illness.
Formal thanks or 'excuse me', used with customers and seniors.
Relief or joy at good news.
When a worry turns out fine.
Young, casual excitement. マジで = seriously.
Said to yourself or friends at the end of the day.
To family or friends; very common.
Reacting to a friend's bad news.

back: I'm so sorry to hear that.
note: Polite sympathy for illness, loss or misfortune.
Telling someone close that you're frightened.

reading: すこしきんちょうしてます
note: Before a speech, interview or first meeting.
Testing the waters after an argument.

term: ああ、なんだかイライラする！
reading: ああなんだかイライラする
note: Venting frustration.
After a slip-up, or when being praised.
Polite relief that someone came through an accident or disaster OK.
